name: Cut appointment no-shows with staged reminders, reply triage and waitlist backfill

parameters.content:
## Cut appointment no-shows end to end

### How it works

One workflow, three connected stages. A schedule trigger reads upcoming appointments and picks a reminder stage per appointment: a heads-up at 48-72 hours, a confirm-or-reschedule ask at 8-48 hours, and a same-day final at 0.5-3 hours. Workflow static data deduplicates, so each appointment gets each stage at most once however often the schedule fires. When a customer answers, the reply webhook classifies the text (English and Dutch keywords) as confirmed, cancel_requested, unclear or no_reply. Confirmed replies mark the appointment. Cancel requests load the freed slot, rank your waitlist by treatment match, flexibility and priority, and send offers to the top three at once, so a cancellation becomes a refill instead of lost revenue.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Disable the demo data nodes and connect your appointment sheet and waitlist sheet (columns are listed in each node).
- [ ] Replace the three placeholder send nodes with WhatsApp Business Cloud, SMS or email nodes.
- [ ] Point your inbound reply webhook at the Webhook node and include appointment_id in the payload (a quick-reply link is the easy way).

### Requirements

- An appointment source with appointment_id, starts_at, channel_preference and contact fields.
- A waitlist with wanted_treatment, flexible and priority_score columns.

### Customization

Reminder bands, keyword regexes, ranking weights, the top-3 offer count and all message copy are plain values in the code nodes.

## 1. Staged reminders
Three time bands, static-data dedup, same-day split onto a priority lane.

## 2. Reply triage
One webhook classifies EN/NL replies into confirmed, cancel, unclear, silent.

## 3. Waitlist backfill
Cancel verdicts rank the waitlist for the freed slot; top 3 get offers.

## 4. Edge cases and response
Unclear or staff-flagged replies end here with a JSON response.
